D021-D022_h001.question:
I’d say this really ramped up over the last six months. I work as a social worker, so I’m in and out of homes all day, and I’ve gotten very rigid about what I’ll eat on the go. I’ve cut out pretty much all bread, pasta, and anything I see as “heavy” or greasy. If lunch at the office is pizza or sandwiches, I’ll just say I already ate and stick to salad or coffee.

Even so, I keep feeling like I need to be smaller. People tell me I don’t need to lose more, but it doesn’t register. If the scale isn’t a little lower than the day before, I panic. I weigh myself multiple times a day, and if the number goes up at all, it’s like I’ve failed.

What’s confusing is that sometimes I completely lose control and eat a lot very quickly, usually alone at night after a stressful day. Afterwards I feel disgusted with myself and I’ll try to “undo” it by making myself throw up or overdoing it at the gym the next morning. Then I go right back to being super strict with food again.
D021-D022_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h001.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h002.question:

I began skipping meals on purpose—first breakfast because “it slows me down,” then a lot of days I’ll push through lunch, too. Sometimes I tell myself I’ll just have one proper meal a day, but even then I’ll cut it down or delay it.

I weigh myself multiple times a day. If the number’s even a little higher, I get this surge of panic, like I’ve messed everything up. I’ll spend ages calculating what I ate, how to “fix” it. I’ve been dropping weight steadily, and people on Discord have commented that I look thinner on camera, but I just feel like it’s never enough.

What complicates it is that there are nights, especially after a stressful trading session, when I completely lose control and eat a ton of food really fast. Afterward I feel disgusted and guilty, and I’ll sometimes make myself get rid of it or try other ways to undo it, then go back to restricting again.
D021-D022_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h002.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h003.question:

I pretty much cut out bread, pasta, rice, anything fried, anything with visible oil. If something looks “heavy” or like it has a lot of carbs or fat, I just can’t make myself eat it. Even looking at pizza in the dining hall makes me anxious, like if I have one slice it’ll instantly show up on my body.

Most days I try to stick to stuff like salad, plain vegetables, maybe some chicken if it doesn’t look greasy. I’ve been tracking everything I eat, and I keep lowering the amount. People have commented that I look like I’ve lost weight, and my clothes are looser, but I’m not really sure what I “should” weigh, so I just keep going.

The weird part is, every couple of weeks I kind of lose control. I’ll be alone, usually at night, and suddenly I’m eating a lot really fast—cereal, cookies, whatever I’ve been avoiding. Afterwards I feel disgusted with myself and sometimes I make myself throw up. Then I go right back to being even stricter the next day.
D021-D022_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h003.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

My foreman mentioned I looked pale and should see a doctor, but I don’t think it’s that serious. I’m still working, still lifting things. I just want to stay in control of my body.

D021-D022_h023.question:
I’ve been struggling with my eating for maybe… the past few months, but it’s gotten more noticeable lately. At work, I’m on my feet all day, so it’s easy to say I’m “too busy” for meals. I’ll just have coffee for breakfast, skip lunch, and then tell my staff I’ll eat later. At home I often pick at dinner or say I already ate at the hospital.

I’m very cautious around certain foods now—anything I think of as “heavy” or high-calorie. If I even imagine eating things like pasta or dessert, I feel this immediate panic that it’ll just turn straight into fat. So I avoid them, or if I do give in, it often turns into me eating much more than I meant to, very quickly, almost on autopilot.

After those episodes, I feel disgusted with myself and desperate to “undo” it—sometimes I make myself sick or overdo it on laxatives, or plan to “make up for it” by not eating the next day. My colleagues have commented that I look “tired” and my husband worries I’m pushing myself too hard, but I keep telling them I’m fine and it’s just the job.

D021-D022_h024.question:
I’ve been struggling with food for about a year now, maybe a bit longer. It started as “clean eating” between shoots, but it’s gotten really rigid. I cut out bread, pasta, rice, anything I think of as “carbs,” and I’m constantly trimming visible fat off meat. On set, when everyone orders pizza or takeout, I’ll say I already ate or that I’m “on a cleanse.” If I even think about touching something like fries or dessert, I get this rush of panic, like I’ll blow up overnight and lose control of how I look on camera or in photos.

The weird part is, it’s not consistent. Every so often—usually late at night after a stressful day or an argument with my ex about our kid—I’ll end up tearing through whatever’s in the kitchen, way past the point of feeling full, like I’m on autopilot. Then I feel disgusted with myself and I’ll force myself to throw up or overdo it with workouts the next morning to “fix” it.

Physically, I’ve noticed I get lightheaded on set, my hair’s thinner, my energy crashes, but I just tell myself it’s the long hours, coffee, and stress of the job and try to push through it.

D021-D022_h025.question:
Honestly, I’m here because my primary doc kept pushing it. I don’t really think it’s that big of a deal. I’ve just been “watching what I eat” more the last… I don’t know, maybe a year? Since my wife passed, I started cutting back. I count pretty much everything now—try to keep it as low as possible. If I go over what I’ve set for myself, I get really uncomfortable, like I’ve done something wrong.

I drive the morning and afternoon routes, so I usually just have coffee before work and maybe something light later. I hate the feeling of being full. The idea of putting on weight really bothers me—I can’t stand seeing my stomach push against my shirt. I weigh myself a lot, just to be sure I’m not creeping up.

Sometimes, though, I’ll come home after the afternoon route and just lose control—eat a bunch of junk in one go, like I’m on autopilot. After that, I panic and try to “fix” it—either by making myself throw up or skipping the next meals and doubling down on cutting back. My daughter and my doctor keep saying they’re worried, but I think they’re overreacting. I’m just trying to stay disciplined.
